Rearranged conditional quantiles from a quantile regression

Source: R/quantile-helpers.R
qr_sorted_quantiles.Rd

Predicted conditional quantiles at each row of newdata, with each row sorted. Sorting is the rearrangement of Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val and Galichon (2010): it makes the conditional quantile function monotone when the quantile regressions cross, and leaves it unchanged when they don't.

Used instead of predict(fit, type = "Fhat"/"Qhat", stepfun = TRUE), which fails when newdata has a single row and returns a non-monotone Fhat when quantiles cross (issue #9).

Usage

qr_sorted_quantiles(fit, newdata)

Arguments

fit

an rqs object (rq() with a vector of tau).

newdata

data frame of covariate values; if missing, the data used to fit the model.

Value

n x length(fit$tau) matrix; row i holds the sorted predicted quantiles for row i of newdata.

References

Chernozhukov, V., I. Fernandez-Val and A. Galichon (2010). “Quantile and Probability Curves Without Crossing.” Econometrica 78(3), 1093-1125.
